- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) and model continues to forecast upward, reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect bearish sentiment.
- Model frequently underestimates prices during prolonged downward sentiment trends; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price movements by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to anticipate 1–2-day lag in price direction.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values to reduce overreaction.
